name: Satya Nadella
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Nadella earned a BS in electrical engineering (1988) and an MS in computer science (1990), worked at Sun Microsystems, and joined Microsoft in 1992 at age ~25 as a staff engineer; his defining rise (cloud leadership, CEO in 2014) came decades later.
early_history_summary: Born in Hyderabad to an IAS officer father and Sanskrit lecturer mother; educated at Hyderabad Public School and Manipal Institute of Technology, then University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (MS CS) before joining Sun and Microsoft.
family_context_summary: Father Bukkapuram Nadella Yugandhar was an Indian Administrative Service officer; mother Prabhavati was a Sanskrit lecturer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were in civil service and academia, not the software industry; domain transfer to Microsoft cloud/OS work is not clearly documented.
evidence_summary: Nadella had a solid engineering education and joined Microsoft by age 25, but no independently distinctive product, research, founding, or public milestone by age 26 is documented. Fame and material executive achievement arrived with cloud leadership and the 2014 CEO appointment (age 46).

name: Sundar Pichai
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Pichai earned a BTech from IIT Kharagpur (1993), then MS (Stanford materials science) and MBA (Wharton); he worked at Applied Materials and McKinsey before joining Google in 2004 at age ~32. Age-26 year was ~1998, during post-grad/early industry years with no dated breakout product or founding.
early_history_summary: Born in Madurai to an electrical engineer father (GEC) and stenographer mother; IIT Kharagpur metallurgical engineering, Stanford MS, Wharton MBA (Siebel/Palmer Scholar), then Applied Materials and McKinsey.
family_context_summary: Father was an electrical engineer at GEC; mother a stenographer; middle-class Tamil family in Chennai/Madurai area.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father’s electrical engineering background is adjacent to technology but not a documented Google product-management apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Strong elite education (IIT, Stanford, Wharton) and early industry roles, but Chrome leadership, Android oversight, and Google/Alphabet CEO roles all occurred well after age 26. No material dated milestone by the cutoff was identified.

name: Jensen Huang
milestone_by_age_26: No material independent milestone by age 26 found. Huang earned a BS from Oregon State (1984) and worked as a microchip designer at AMD and LSI Logic; the Sun GX graphics accelerator he worked on with Malachowsky and Priem was finalized around 1989 (age ~26) as employee work. He co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 at age 30—the defining milestone.
early_history_summary: Born in Taipei; childhood in Taiwan and Thailand; sent to Oneida Baptist Institute in Kentucky then Aloha High School in Oregon; dishwasher/busboy at Denny’s; OSU electrical engineering; Stanford MS while working; AMD then LSI before NVIDIA.
family_context_summary: Middle-class Taiwanese family; father a chemical engineer at an oil refinery, mother a schoolteacher; family sold possessions to fund US schooling.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were engineer and teacher, not semiconductor-graphics entrepreneurs; no inherited industry platform documented.
evidence_summary: By age 26 Huang was a capable chip designer (AMD/LSI) involved in successful graphics work for Sun, but his material, independently defining achievement—co-founding and leading NVIDIA—occurred at age 30 in 1993. Employee product work does not meet the bar used for founder-scale milestones.

name: Lisa Su
milestone_by_age_26: No material public milestone by age 26 found. Su completed MIT BS/MS/PhD in electrical engineering (PhD 1994, age ~24–25), joined TI then IBM research staff (1995, age ~25). Copper interconnect commercial launch was 1998 (age ~28–29); MIT TR35 recognition ~2001–2002; AMD CEO 2014 (age 44).
early_history_summary: Born in Tainan, Taiwan; immigrated to Queens at age 3; Bronx High School of Science; MIT triple EE degree path with early SOI MOSFET research; TI then IBM device-physics research.
family_context_summary: Taiwanese immigrant family in Queens; father worked as a statistician for NYC government; mother an accountant who later became an entrepreneur; cousin of Jensen Huang.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents encouraged math/science and business concepts; not semiconductor executives themselves.
evidence_summary: Elite MIT training and early IBM hire by age 25 are strong career starts, but the copper technology launch, TR35 recognition, Freescale CTO role, and AMD CEO turnaround all post-date age 26. PhD completion alone is not treated as a material breakout milestone.

name: Fei-Fei Li
milestone_by_age_26: No material career-defining milestone by age 26 found. Li earned a Princeton BA (1999) and was a Caltech PhD student through 2005; a PNAS paper appeared in 2002 near age 26, but ImageNet (begun ~2007, age ~31), Stanford faculty rise, and Google Cloud AI leadership came later. Fame as ImageNet creator arrived well after the cutoff.
early_history_summary: Born in Beijing, raised in Chengdu; immigrated to New Jersey as a teen; worked in family dry-cleaning business while at Parsippany High and Princeton; Caltech PhD under Pietro Perona and Christof Koch (2005).
family_context_summary: Chinese immigrant family that ran a dry-cleaning business in New Jersey; modest means; Li worked weekends at the shop and as a dishwasher.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family ran a small service business, not academic AI; no inherited research network documented.
evidence_summary: Strong early education and graduate research by the mid-20s, but the project that made her globally known—ImageNet and ILSVRC—began when she was about 31. Conservative coding treats pre-ImageNet student publications as insufficient for age-26 eligibility.

name: Andrew Ng
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored the seminal Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) paper with David Blei and Michael I. Jordan, presented at NIPS 2001 (age 25), and received his Berkeley PhD under Jordan before joining Stanford as assistant professor in 2002 (age 26).
early_history_summary: Born in London to Hong Kong immigrant parents (father a hematologist/UCL lecturer; mother arts administrator); raised partly in Hong Kong and Singapore (Raffles Institution); triple major at Carnegie Mellon (1997); MIT MS (1998) building an early automated research-paper search engine; Berkeley PhD (2002) under Michael Jordan with reinforcement-learning thesis and LDA collaboration.
family_context_summary: Parents emigrated from Hong Kong; father Ronald Paul Ng was a hematologist and UCL Medical School lecturer; mother Tisa Ho worked in arts administration (London Film Festival).
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were highly educated professionals (medicine/academia and arts) providing cultural capital and educational emphasis, but not ML/AI domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CMU triple major, MIT MS, Berkeley under Michael Jordan, LDA, Stanford faculty, Bell Labs research
evidence_summary: Ng stacked elite pipelines (CMU, MIT, Berkeley under Michael Jordan) and produced foundational ML research by his mid-20s, including LDA at NIPS 2001 and a Stanford CS faculty appointment by 2002. Early Bell Labs research and an MIT paper-search prototype show sustained technical reps. Family provided educated professional support rather than AI-domain apprenticeship. Later Google Brain, Coursera, and Baidu roles built on this early academic breakout.
starting_point: Born in London to Hong Kong immigrant parents; father a hematologist/academic, mother an arts administrator; childhood in Hong Kong and Singapore with elite secondary schooling at Raffles Institution.
current_position: AI entrepreneur and educator; founder of DeepLearning.AI and LandingAI, chair of AI Fund, Amazon board member (since 2024), Stanford adjunct professor; widely known for Coursera ML courses reaching millions.

trajectory.event: Graduated Carnegie Mellon with a triple major in computer science, statistics, and economics; conducted early research at AT&T Bell Labs.
Earned MIT MS and built an early automatically indexed web search engine for research papers (CiteSeer precursor).
Co-authored Latent Dirichlet Allocation with Blei and Jordan, presented at NIPS—foundational topic modeling work.
Received Berkeley PhD under Michael Jordan and joined Stanford as assistant professor of computer science.
Founded Google Brain with Jeff Dean and others, scaling deep learning on Google infrastructure.
Co-founded Coursera with Daphne Koller; machine-learning MOOC became a global education phenomenon.
Joined Baidu as chief scientist leading large-scale AI research teams.
Appointed to Amazon’s board of directors amid ongoing AI Fund and LandingAI work.

name: Dario Amodei
milestone_by_age_26: No material AI/industry milestone by age 26 found. Amodei was a USA Physics Olympiad team member (2000, ~age 17) and earned a Hertz Fellowship (2007) while pursuing a Princeton biophysics PhD completed in 2011 (~age 28). Baidu/Google/OpenAI roles and Anthropic founding (2021, ~age 38) all came later.
early_history_summary: Born in San Francisco; Lowell High School; Caltech then Stanford physics BS; Princeton biophysics PhD (2011) on neural-circuit electrophysiology under Berry/Bialek; postdoc at Stanford Medicine before industry AI roles.
family_context_summary: Father Riccardo Amodei was an Italian-American leather craftsman who died when Dario was a young adult; mother Elena Engel is a Jewish American library project manager.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were craftsman and library professional—not AI researchers; no inherited AI domain platform.
evidence_summary: Early physics talent (USAPhO team) and elite PhD training are documented, but by age 26 he was still a graduate student without a public AI product, company, or industry leadership milestone. OpenAI VP research and Anthropic co-founding occurred in his 30s.

name: Daniela Amodei
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. After UCSC English BA and brief political work, she joined Stripe around 2013 (~age 26) as an early recruiting hire—solid career start but not a dated product/founding breakout. OpenAI safety/policy VP and Anthropic co-founding (2021, ~age 34) came later.
early_history_summary: Born in San Francisco in 1987; sister of Dario Amodei; Lowell High School; classical flute scholarship; BA English literature UC Santa Cruz; congressional campaign and House staff work before tech.
family_context_summary: Same family as Dario: craftsman father (deceased when she was a young adult) and library project-manager mother; San Francisco upbringing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as AI or tech-industry family domain advantage.
evidence_summary: Early Stripe employment near age 26 as a recruiter is not treated as a material independent milestone comparable to product launches or research breakthroughs. Defining roles at OpenAI and Anthropic occurred after age 30.

name: Mira Murati
category: AI executive (OpenAI CTO; Thinking Machines Lab CEO)
milestone_by_age_26: No material AI milestone by age 26 found. Murati joined Tesla in 2013 (~age 24) as a product manager on Model X—strong early career role, but Model X launch and her fame as OpenAI CTO (2022) and Thinking Machines Lab founder (2025) came after age 26 (cutoff ~Dec 2014). OpenAI joined 2018 (~age 29).
early_history_summary: Born in Vlorë, Albania; Pearson College UWC (Canada) at 16; dual Colby BA (2011) and Dartmouth BEng (2012); Goldman Sachs Tokyo internship; Zodiac Aerospace; Tesla PM then Leap Motion before OpenAI.
family_context_summary: Albanian upbringing; emigrated for UWC high school in Canada; family financial details not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Tesla product-management role by the mid-20s is a strong industry start, but it is not the independently defining, public AI milestone associated with her later reputation. OpenAI CTO leadership of ChatGPT-era products and Thinking Machines Lab founding occurred in her 30s.

name: Paul Graham
milestone_by_age_26: No material entrepreneurial milestone by age 26 found. Graham earned a Cornell BA (1986) and Harvard CS MS/PhD (1990, age ~25–26); On Lisp was published 1993 (age ~28–29) and Viaweb founded 1995–96 (age ~31). Y Combinator began in 2005 (age ~40).
early_history_summary: Born in Weymouth, England; father Welsh nuclear engineer at Westinghouse; family moved to Pittsburgh; Gateway High School; Cornell philosophy; Harvard CS PhD; also studied painting at RISD and Accademia di Belle Arti Florence.
family_context_summary: Father from Wales worked for Westinghouse designing nuclear reactors; family relocated from England to Pittsburgh in 1968.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a nuclear engineer—technical household but not software/startup domain.
evidence_summary: Harvard PhD by ~26 is elite academic progress, but the career-defining Viaweb founding/sale and Y Combinator co-founding both occurred after age 30. Lisp books and essays that built his reputation also clustered after the age-26 cutoff.

name: Jessica Livingston
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Livingston graduated Phillips Academy (1989) and Bucknell (English BA), then held varied marketing/finance roles (Fidelity, Food & Wine, consulting, wedding planning, investment-bank VP). Y Combinator co-founding in 2005 was at age ~34; Founders at Work published 2007.
early_history_summary: Born in Minneapolis; raised largely by father and grandmother in the Boston area; Phillips Academy then Bucknell English; series of early career jobs before meeting Graham/Morris/Blackwell and co-founding YC.
family_context_summary: Raised largely by father and grandmother after relocating from Minneapolis to the Boston area; further family financial details not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as startup/VC family domain.
evidence_summary: By age 26 Livingston was in ordinary post-college employment without a dated founding, investment, or publishing breakthrough. Y Combinator (2005) and Founders at Work (2007) define her public career well after the cutoff.

name: Guido van Rossum
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Van Rossum won IMO bronze in 1974 (age 18) and earned a University of Amsterdam master’s in mathematics and computer science in 1982 (age ~26). He began Python as a Christmas hobby project in December 1989 at age 33 while at CWI; first public release and later fame as Python’s creator came after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in The Hague, Netherlands; IMO bronze 1974; University of Amsterdam master’s 1982; worked at CWI on ABC language and BSD Unix glob(); later NIST, CNRI, BeOpen, Zope, Google, Dropbox, Microsoft.
family_context_summary: Dutch upbringing; brother Just van Rossum is a type designer (designed Python Powered logo typeface). Broader family financial/domain details not documented.
evidence_summary: IMO bronze shows early mathematical talent, and a 1982 master’s at ~26 is solid academic completion, but Python—the achievement that defines his global impact—was started at age 33 in late 1989. Age-26 eligibility requires a material milestone tied to the success path; that is not present here.
